issue:commit.description: Create a git commit with an AI-generated message. Use -k for the ticket key, or the key is auto-detected from the branch name. When -k differs from the branch-embedded ticket key, warns and prompts to pick a value interactively, or fails hard with both keys shown when non-interactive; --dry-run only warns. Fails hard if .gitignore is staged. Blank AI commit responses fail fast with provider-aware diagnostics. When a code review or plan artifact already exists for the ticket, its summary is used to scope the commit message automatically. Use --source <plan-stem|ticket-key> to point at a specific review artifact; the lookup probes the tracker directory first, then the custom directory, and finds the artifact in any supported format (json|md|yaml|yml). When no exact artifact matches, the plan manifests (.sources.json) in both directories are matched by ticket key, custom plan name, source name, hash, or plan stem and the matched plan's review artifact is used (a token matching several plans logs a warning and is skipped); then the tracker and custom directories are scanned for date-prefixed variants (YYYY-MM-DD-<token>-review.<ext> or the running repository's scoped YYYY-MM-DD-<token>-<repo-basename>-review.<ext>; other repositories' scoped artifacts are ignored) and the newest by mtime wins on ambiguity with a warning. When no fresh diff-grounded commit description exists for the staged diff, one is generated inline. When running from source, use yarn start issue:commit --conventional.

issue:generate.description: Generate ticket descriptions from local files, repo-scoped artifacts via --repos, URLs, or ticket keys. Tracker browse URLs (e.g., https://<org>.atlassian.net/browse/<KEY>) are automatically detected and fetched via the tracker REST API instead of scraping HTML; self-hosted instances are supported when atlassian.baseUrl is configured. Local .md, .json, .yaml, and .yml files that parse as tickets are imported as tickets; files that are not recognized as ticket-formatted content remain plain file sources. Repo-scoped generation inspects prior plan artifacts anywhere under ~/.wf/<repo>/**/* and correlates them by keyword similarity so synthesis prompts can reuse earlier implementation context. When multiple repos are supplied, the synthesis prompt also compares repo conventions, including linter and formatter rules, and git-hook tools across checkouts. AI synthesis always runs on every source to enrich and standardize the output. The AI is instructed to return a structured JSON object (title, type, priority, description) that is validated against the ticket schema before conversion to the requested output format. When agent or CLI backends are used, the provider session ID is threaded across oversized-source summarisation, clarification, and synthesis so all calls share coherent context. Generated output enforces formal writing conventions (concise prose, no contractions, active voice, British English) before display or save. Blank AI generate-stage responses fail fast with provider-aware diagnostics. Can use an agent backend when stages.generate.backend is set to agent

issue:implement.description: Carry out an implementation plan from a ticket-backed, hashed, or custom plan artifact. Delegates the generate-and-verify loop to the configured backend (Anthropic Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, or Claude CLI headless mode) based on stages.implement.provider and stages.implement.backend. In auto model-routing mode, optional stages.implement.modelRoutingThresholds can send medium/high-complexity plans to the mechanical model when targeted writes or plan steps exceed configured limits; targeted writes are concrete affectedFiles entries, not affectedFilesContext entries. Use --model-routing default or --model-routing mechanical to override automatic selection. Progress events are streamed to the terminal so you can follow task and tool activity while edits are being generated. All backends emit stable task and tool progress lines plus explicit file mutation logs and verification logs so terminal output stays human-readable while the agent works. Verification commands are expected to be repo-root-relative; stale plan artifacts that still embed redundant repo-selection `cd` prefixes are normalized, while cross-repo directory jumps are treated as setup errors. A verification step may set earlyExitPattern to a valid regex; when stdout or stderr matches it, wf records the check as passed and terminates the command process group, while steps without it run to normal completion. Set stages.implement.provider and stages.implement.backend in wf.config to select the backend. Use backend: agent with provider anthropic or openai for the Agent SDK path, or backend: cli with provider anthropic or openai for the CLI headless mode (Claude CLI or Codex CLI respectively). Set stages.implement.timeoutMs to override the wall-clock subprocess timeout (default: 15 minutes) and stages.implement.inactivityTimeoutMs to override the per-message inactivity timeout (default: 2 minutes). For the Codex CLI backend, only command execution, file changes, and tool calls reset the inactivity timer — plain agent-text messages do not, and ten consecutive text-only messages abort the run early as a stall regardless of either timeout. Set stages.implement.stallThresholdForVerificationFix to override how many consecutive no-write or non-improving verification fix passes the Claude CLI and Codex CLI backends attempt before stopping (default: 2). The Claude CLI, Anthropic Agent SDK, and OpenAI Agents SDK backends also end the continuation loop after 2 consecutive passes that write no files, touch nothing git-visible, and declare nothing; an agent that finds a planned file already satisfies the plan can emit a `NO-CHANGE: <path>` line in its pass summary, which removes that file from the unvisited set and is listed as agent-declared in the file summary (declarations are ignored for unplanned, glob, or actually edited files). Declarations tolerate bold, quotes, backticks, a trailing period, and any keyword casing, but a comma-separated list or a missing colon is ignored; repeating an already accepted declaration does not count as progress. Plan-step verification fix prompts also tell the agent to answer a step whose target is already absent with a single-line proof plus `NO-CHANGE: <path>` instead of re-reading files. The Anthropic backend explicitly loads ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and the repository-root CLAUDE.md, warning when either file is missing. The OpenAI backend loads ~/.openai/AGENTS.md and the repository-root AGENTS.md with the same warning behavior and only exposes an exact-match verify_command tool for whitelisted verification commands. When running from source, use `yarn start issue:implement ...` for the implementation stage and `yarn start issue:commit --conventional` to stage the final conventional commit once the work is accepted. Unsupported providers (google, deepseek) fail fast with a clear error listing supported providers. backend: standard is rejected at runtime because the implement stage requires an agent-capable backend. Blank AI findings responses fail fast with provider-aware diagnostics instead of generic parse errors. Repo conventions are detected up front and threaded into every backend prompt, including continuation passes, so formatter and structural ESLint constraints survive context compaction. Plan complexity is computed deterministically from plan size (targeted writes, steps, phases, new repositories) combined with the highest model-assessed risk severity; the model does not estimate it. A complexity-gated commit policy controls whether the backend may self-commit: low-complexity plans permit a single commit; medium and high plans block commits and rewind any self-made commits via git reset --soft, re-staging the content so issue:commit handles the final message. Enforcement always runs even if the backend throws, and any git safety-check failure (shallow repo, detached HEAD, missing upstream) is logged and treated as a skip rather than an error. Rename and removal work is verified against the needle: every backend is told to search it case-insensitively across the whole repository (docs, specs, config, env files and CI included) until zero matches remain, and the OpenAI search tool skips binary files, node_modules, dist and .git. Plan entries with status `to-delete` are orphaned files the agent should delete; the Anthropic Agent SDK backend provides a path-guarded DeleteFile tool, and a deleted file counts as done in the continuation loop. Run issue:fetch then issue:plan before calling this command for ticket-backed workflows. When a hashed plan artifact is provided, the action is inferred from the filename/manifest and `--action` becomes optional, but any supplied action is still validated against the resolved artifact. Before implementation, the command runs an interactive branch creation workflow: prompts to create a new branch or stay on the current one, then only checks the working tree for uncommitted changes when a pull is needed. When staying on the current branch, the user is asked whether to pull; stashing is only triggered if a pull is accepted. When creating a new branch, uncommitted changes are stashed before pulling the source branch (dev or main). After each pull, runs a dependency install via the detected package manager (bun, pnpm, yarn, or npm); use --skip-install to suppress. The install is skipped automatically, with no warning, when the repo has no package.json (e.g. Terraform-only repos). Failures are surfaced as warnings and never abort the command. Generated branch names exceeding 100 characters are automatically truncated at the nearest word boundary. Use --silent to auto-stash without prompting; branch selection and naming still prompt when a TTY is available. Use --no-branch to skip branch creation and work directly on the current branch. Use --branch-name-pattern to override the enforced branch name validation regex from git.branchNamePattern config. Branch names are validated when the branch is created, against git ref conventions and the resolved naming pattern (--branch-name-pattern, else git.branchNamePattern, else built-in patterns). Names entered at the branch prompt are trimmed, a pasted `git checkout -b`/`git switch -c` prefix is stripped, and input is validated inline with the specific rejection reason. When branch creation still rejects a name, interactive runs log the reason to the agent log and reopen the branch-name prompt instead of aborting; non-interactive runs fail fast. An invalid --branch-name-pattern regex is rejected before any work starts, and an invalid git.branchNamePattern regex fails config validation at startup. When running against multiple repos, repos absent from the plan's affectedRepositories and newRepositories are skipped with a log message. When a plan declares newRepositories, those repos are scaffolded as sibling directories and prepended to the execution order so they run before existing repos. Plan-step verification runs by default; set stages.implement.planStepVerification.enabled to false to turn it off, and it skips itself with a log line when there are no changes, no assessed steps, a new repo, or a commit policy that allows direct commits. When it runs, a post-implementation AI auditor re-reads the diff and scores each plan step as done, partially-done, not-done, not-applicable, or unverifiable. Terminal done, not-applicable, and unverifiable verdicts are sticky and never reassessed; only pending steps receive another fidelity pre-pass and fix round. A finding that survives one targeted fix round is suppressed with a WARN log and summary count. Each assessor prompt renders its example response from the real [Plan step N] indices being assessed and tells the model never to renumber from 0; a reply with an index outside the assessed set, or none of the expected indices, fails the attempt (logged as `step-verify.assess.attempt-failed`) and is retried once instead of being filled in as not-done, while a single omitted index still falls back to not-done. stages.implement.planStepVerification.stallWindow (default: 3) uses the pending-count window to stop a remaining pending set that no longer shrinks. stages.implement.planStepVerification.mode selects the assessor strategy; when omitted, wf routes automatically: high-complexity plans use pull, low-complexity plans use push, and medium-complexity plans use push when the measured diff fits the push evidence budget and pull when it exceeds it; the choice and its reason are logged as step-verify.mode=<mode> (<reason>), and auto routing falls back to push when the assessor provider is not anthropic or openai. An explicit push or pull always wins. push collects git diff evidence and, when verification commands ran during implementation, injects a ## Command execution evidence section listing their outcomes, the commit policy, staged files, and commit count — allowing command-execution plan steps to be assessed as done or not-done rather than unverifiable; pull spawns an agent with live repository access via chatTurn so the assessor can read files directly, is given a host-built ## Mandatory inspection checklist of every changed and untracked file plus the ## Command execution evidence section, and must list the files it inspected in inspectedPaths; a done or not-applicable step that names a checklist file missing from inspectedPaths is downgraded to unverifiable (step-verify.pull.coverage-gap), and an empty inspectedPaths for a non-empty checklist fails the attempt. A pull provider outside anthropic or openai ends only the verification run (step-verify.error), not the implement workflow. stages.implement.planStepVerification.provider and .model override the provider and model used by the assessor; provider must be anthropic or openai when mode is pull. When only .model is set without .provider, the implement stage provider is used. stages.implement.planStepVerification.backend overrides the AI backend used by both the step assessor and the spec-fidelity pre-pass; valid values are agent, cli, and standard. When set alongside provider and model, the named backend is used instead of the default implement-stage backend; omit to inherit it. Push mode sizes its diff evidence from the measured changeset instead of fixed per-file caps: evidence up to 60k characters is sent whole, and up to 240k characters (including the changed-files list) is still sent whole in one call. Larger changesets are assessed in phases, one call per group of steps, each with the full changed-files list and uncut diffs of the files its steps name (logged as step-verify.assess.phased). A file counts as named by a step only when its whole repo-relative path appears in the step text (an optional leading ./ is accepted), so a step naming src/a.tsx no longer pulls in src/a.ts; this applies to phased grouping, evidence prioritisation, the spec-fidelity diff budget, and the pull-mode coverage-gap check. Only a group that still cannot fit is cut to head and tail slices with an Evidence completeness section, a gap-aware unverifiable rule, and WARN logs (step-verify.evidence.over-ceiling, step-verify.diff.truncated, step-verify.diff.omitted, step-verify.unverifiable.evidence-gap); the spec-fidelity pre-pass applies the same allocation to its diff with a 120k ceiling and logs step-fidelity.diff.truncated. step-verify.evidence.budget is always logged. Codex CLI uses codex exec --output-schema with a temporary schema file. Assessed and complete events include done, not-applicable, partially-done, and not-done counts plus unverifiable counts. The fallback is logged once as `ai.model.fallback`. Before each verification round, a spec-fidelity pre-pass runs one sequential AI call per assessed step to detect literal claim deviations — regex patterns, required parameters, exact threshold values, and string literals — against the diff. The fidelity pre-pass uses the same planStepVerification.provider, .model, and .backend overrides as the step assessor, falling back to the implement-stage provider and backend when none are configured. Steps with confirmed concrete mismatches receive a [SPEC FIDELITY ERRORS] annotation that causes the step assessor to score them partially-done and enter a fix round even when the code looks superficially complete. Warning-severity findings (diff is silent on a claim) are surfaced but do not trigger a fix round. When a plan step carries an `intent`, the pre-pass adds it to the prompt for that step, and a literal that differs from the diff is downgraded to a warning when the diff still satisfies the stated intent (only intents checkable from the diff count); per-repo step filtering keeps each intent with its step because the intent lives on the step object, and steps without an `intent` behave as before. an agent that cannot or should not implement a step as written can add a final-message line `PLAN-PROBLEM: <step number from the Plan steps list> | <reason> | <what you did instead>` (exactly three non-empty parts; bold, bullet, backticks, `Step N` and any casing are tolerated; out-of-range steps and malformed lines are ignored with a WARN log; the first report per step wins; text is capped at 500 characters and 20 reports per run). Reports are accepted on every backend (Codex reads only its final message), printed as `Plan problem reported for step N`, saved as run.planProblems in the newest implement-verification run file, shown to the spec-fidelity auditor and to the fix-round prompts, and listed in the review context; under `wf issue` with a saved session, plan problems and blocking spec-fidelity deviations are also stored per repo in the `records` of the implement stage in the session file (deduplicated, at most 20 per repo, 500 characters each) and passed to the review stage as a labelled data block in its prior-stage context; the auditor still judges whether the alternative is sound, and verification commands remain the hard gate. Only the spec-fidelity pre-pass reads intents; the step assessor sees step text alone. The pre-pass is skipped when the diff is empty and never throws; any internal error is silently swallowed so the verification loop is unaffected. Ordinary review-stage chat requests remain unstructured unless they explicitly provide a response schema, so they do not inherit the review schema accidentally. Runs a Figma implementation pass when stages.implement.figma is true or --figma is passed; Figma frame links stored in the plan manifest by issue:plan are re-read at implement time to fetch design context via the Figma REST API, injecting frame name, dimensions, and screenshot URL into the backend prompt so the implementer can reconcile generated code against spacing, colour, and component-structure constraints before committing. The manifest is resolved directly from the ticket artifact path so the correct links are always loaded without a branch-name search. Figma frame URLs that lack a `?node-id=` query parameter are skipped with a WARN rather than generating a malformed API call. If all frame fetches fail despite valid links being present, a WARN is written to the on-disk agent log to distinguish network or token failures from the links-absent case.When the plan artifact lists uiDesignScreenshots (set by issue:plan --ui-design-screenshots), the Anthropic agent backend adds their paths to the task brief and grants the sandbox read access to each parent directory (logged), and the Claude CLI backend passes each parent directory with --add-dir and repeats a one-line reminder on continuation passes; the OpenAI agent backend cannot show images and logs a warning. The design conformance check is off by default; it runs when stages.implement.designConformance.enabled is true, or automatically when wf issue is started with --ui-design-screenshots, which switches the check on even when enabled is false and merges it with the rest of stages.implement.designConformance (maxScreenshots, provider, model, backend). Without the flag the config alone decides: enabled true runs the check and enabled false or unset does not. The flag only requests the check; the screenshots still come from the plan artifact, so a run started past the plan stage against a plan stored without them reports that the check was skipped. It adds an advisory check after verification: one sequential AI call per screenshot (capped by designConformance.maxScreenshots) compares the implement diff against that image, and any deviations are printed under Design conformance (advisory), logged as design-check, and saved as run.designConformance in the newest implement-verification run file. The check never fails the run. Its target follows the same override rules as planStepVerification: designConformance.provider, .model and .backend override the implement stage target, and each one that is unset falls back to stages.implement (.model alone uses the implement stage provider; .provider requires .model). The backend selects how the call runs. standard sends the screenshot as an inline image through the provider API (anthropic or openai). cli runs the Claude CLI (anthropic) or Codex CLI (openai) with the screenshot path in the prompt, and agent runs the Anthropic Agent SDK with the screenshot directory readable; the OpenAI agent backend cannot read images, so it is skipped with a warning, as is any provider other than anthropic or openai. designConformance accepts only enabled, maxScreenshots, provider, model, and backend.

issue:plan.description: Plan ticket implementation from a local artifact or repo-scoped custom artifact. If a local artifact is not found, the command will attempt to fetch it from the primary tracker. Use --force to fetch and recreate artifacts. Repo-scoped planning inspects prior plan artifacts anywhere under ~/.wf/<repo>/**/* and correlates them by keyword similarity so planning prompts can reuse earlier implementation context. Planning prompts include detected repository test conventions and ecosystem-specific verification guidance so generated steps match local test patterns and only reference allowed command forms. Node verification commands use the detected package manager: npm uses `npm run <script> -- <args>`, yarn uses `yarn <script> <args>`, pnpm uses `pnpm run <script> <args>`, and bun uses `bun run <script> <args>`; the same syntax is used by validation and retry guidance. When a design system is detected, observed element class conventions (e.g. h1–h6 heading classes, grid-gap token choices, responsive grid-cols breakpoint tiers mined from real .vue/.tsx files) are included in the plan prompt; the design-system block is omitted for non-UI tickets so the prompt stays focused. Existing components and composables whose names share significant vocabulary with the ticket are surfaced in the plan prompt as reuse candidates so the planner can reference them before creating new files; repos that place UI files outside `app/components` or `app/composables` receive no candidates. Generated plans are semantically validated before they are saved: wf retries once with explicit repair feedback when a draft omits rename targets, uses a non-allowlisted verification command, or contradicts detected test conventions. Steps that delete, drop, remove, replace or rename a term also need a case-insensitive zero-match verification command such as `bash -c '! git grep -I -i -q -F <term>'` (or a `needle-search-required` waiver); a missing or `\\b`-only check is reported as an advisory quality risk after the repair retry. A step that writes a spec with a mocked collaborator must also state that the collaborator is asserted called after the act step (or carry a `test-call-assertion-required` waiver); this is reported the same advisory way. Each plan step is an object with a `description` and an optional `intent`: the planner is told to emit an intent only for steps that prescribe a literal (a call chain, signature, regex or test name), phrased as a goal checkable from the diff; legacy artifacts with flat string `steps` and an index-aligned `stepIntents` array are combined into step objects on load, a length mismatch between the legacy arrays fails plan validation, and markdown artifacts store each intent as an `Intent:` line directly under its numbered step. The planner is told to search the needle case-insensitively across the whole repository, including docs, specs, config, env files and CI, and may mark orphaned files it deletes with the `to-delete` file status (rejected in affectedFilesContext). A step that names two config keys (backticked or quoted, starting with `ai.`, `stages.`, `git.` or `figma.`) with the same final segment, or that adds a `resolve*`, `get*`, `pick*`, `select*` or `build*` function, is checked against the repository with `git grep`; when an existing resolver in a file the plan does not list already reads those keys or defines that name, the plan records a `duplicate-resolver` risk ("reuse <name> in <file>:<line>, or state why it cannot be reused") without a repair retry. The lookup is skipped when no repository directory is known and fails open on any git error. Targeted verification commands are interpreted as repo-root-relative: redundant `cd <repo>` prefixes are normalized away, while commands that change directories outside the selected repository are rejected. When `--figma` is passed or `stages.plan.figma` is `true`, Figma frame links found in the ticket description or acceptance criteria are extracted with their full query strings (including `?node-id=` parameters) and stored in the plan manifest, enabling Figma REST API design context injection during a later `issue:implement --figma` run and `issue:review --figma` run. When no inline Figma links are found but a design system is detected in the repo, an interactive prompt asks for frame links in TTY sessions; links supplied this way are stored in the manifest but are not threaded into the AI generation context.

issue:review.description: AI-powered code review of local changes, ticket-associated pull requests, or PR diffs. Each review includes nested trace provenance, issue-local suggestions, and diff-aligned inline comment anchors. Ticket-keyed reviews are cached to `<ticket>-review.<format>`, where the format comes from `-f/--format` or `stages.review.outputFormat` (default md); a cached artifact is served regardless of the format it was written in, and regenerating with `--force` under a different format replaces the stale variant so each ticket keeps exactly one review artifact. In multi-repo runs the artifact gains a repo-scope suffix — `<ticket>-<repo-basename>-review.<ext>`, one file per repository — so each repo's cached result is stored independently and the first repository's cached review is never served to subsequent repositories in the same run; mono-repo runs stay unscoped so the artifact shares its stem with the commit-description sidecar. The review rubric includes Accessibility (roles, focus states, screen-reader operability), Scope & necessity (replaces the former separate Scope and Necessity criteria), and Pattern grounding (checks flagged patterns against actual codebase conventions before raising an issue) among its default criteria. The verdict follows risk-adjusted severity: each issue carries a `risk` (the probability, 0 to 1, that it manifests in reality) that weights its severity, and a review that contains any issue still at `error` after risk adjustment is recorded as Changes requested even when the model returned `approved: true`. Issues at warning or info after risk adjustment do not block approval; an issue without a risk keeps its reported severity. Reviews are enriched with detected repo conventions (linter, formatter, language, TypeScript config) and structured verification results; for eligible PR and single-repository reviews, lint, typecheck, and test run live in an invocation-scoped disposable git worktree after the exact reviewed diff is applied, leaving the target repository untouched. Verification records passed, failed, or not-run status and are persisted beside the review in Markdown, JSON, and YAML output. Use `--skip-verification` to bypass it. Blank or blocked AI review responses fail fast with provider-aware diagnostics instead of generic parse errors; Codex CLI schema/configuration rejections preserve the provider detail and are not reported as rate-limit failures. Runs the SonarQube CLI (`sonar analyze secrets` then `sonar analyze`) when `stages.review.sonar` is `true` or `--sonar` is passed; requires `sonar` on PATH and an authenticated `sonar auth status`. Scopes the scan to staged changes when present, otherwise to the merge-base diff against a source branch recovered from `--session-id`, a locally-persisted session for `--ticket-key`, a plan manifest, git reflog, or an interactive prompt, in that order. A bare `--ticket-key` with no matching local session, or any run where no base branch can be resolved, falls back to an unscoped `sonar analyze` and logs a WARN entry to the on-disk log with context `sonar-stage`; a recorded source-branch lookup that fails (for example an unreadable session directory) logs a WARN with the same context and the scan falls back to the development or upstream branch. Findings are reported and logged at WARN with context `sonar-scanner`, and review continues; a clean scan is confirmed too, both on the console and in the persisted log (at INFO), so it stays distinguishable from a scan that never ran; a missing CLI or auth/project misconfiguration continues the review without Sonar findings, leaving other targets in the same run unaffected. That failure warning is always logged at WARN with context `sonar-stage` and is not hidden by `--silent`. Use `--sonar-only` to run only the SonarQube scan for local repositories; it skips AI review, verification, Figma, comments, and chat, prints findings directly, exits 0 for clean or finding-bearing scans, and propagates scan/setup failures through the normal error handler. CLI-backed review sessions send a final human-readable epilogue after parsing the JSON review; Claude CLI forks that epilogue session, while Codex CLI resumes the same session because its JSON exec path has no fork flag. Runs a Figma design-conformance check when `stages.review.figma` is `true` or `--figma` is passed; Figma frame links captured from the ticket description during `issue:plan` are stored in the plan manifest and re-read at review time to fetch design context via the Figma REST API, injecting frame name, dimensions, and screenshot URL into the review prompt so the reviewer model can evaluate visual conformance against the original frames. If all frame fetches fail despite valid links being present, a WARN is written to the on-disk agent log to distinguish network or token failures from the links-absent case. When `--ui-design-screenshots` was passed to `issue:plan` or `issue`, the resolved screenshot paths are stored in the plan artifact; at review time those paths are re-read and handed to the reviewer — base64-encoded as multimodal prompt content for API-backed providers, or as filesystem paths appended to the prompt (with each screenshot directory granted via `--add-dir`) for the Claude CLI backend — so the reviewer can check UI conformance against the original design files. When the review diff exceeds the summarisation threshold (default 80 000 chars), oversized per-file patches are batched into as few CLI calls as possible — grouping files within a 60 000-character chunk budget — rather than one call per file; each batch call returns `=== FILE: <path> ===`-delimited summaries and paths are normalised on both sides to avoid OS separator mismatches. Configure `stages.review.maxDiffLength` (integer ≥ 1) to override the 80 000-character threshold and `stages.review.epilogueTimeoutMs` (integer ≥ 0, default 30 000 ms) to adjust the CLI epilogue spawn timeout. Epilogue failures from `is_error` responses or spawn errors are surfaced in the console log with the first line of the extracted diagnostic so the root cause is visible without opening a log file.
